findings.problem: Line 6 says Paul and Barnabas are driven out "and the disciples are STILL filled with joy", then jokes "Somebody runs ME out of town... These disciples? JOY." Acts 13:52 says only "And the disciples were filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit." The text doesn't say who "the disciples" are (the new believers left in Pisidian Antioch, or Paul and Barnabas), and it doesn't link their joy to being driven out with a "still" or "in spite of". The line and the joke treat the disciples as the ones run out of town and make the joy a reaction to that.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open. Who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Line 1 says Paul "squeezes Israel's WHOLE history into it". In Acts 13:17-25, Paul's history runs from the fathers and Egypt through David, then jumps to John and Jesus. It isn't Israel's whole history, so this stretches the text in a statement about Scripture, not in a joke. Something like "squeezes centuries of Israel's history into it" would stay true.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.
